title: Kroger to lay off 3,000 corporate employees over 3 years as it leans into artificial intelligence
source_used: Associated Press (text read through its copy on Bozeman Daily Chronicle); Grocery Dive for the memo details
key_facts: Kroger will lay off 3,000 corporate employees over the next three years as it ramps up its use of artificial intelligence to streamline operations (AP).
CEO Greg Foran wrote the plan in a memo to employees on Monday (12 Oct 2026); AP quotes him as saying the company must 'reduce duplicative work'.
Kroger is the largest standalone US supermarket chain, based in Cincinnati, with 409,000 employees and more than 2,700 stores (AP).
Foran, a former head of Walmart's US division, became Kroger's CEO in February, 11 months after the previous CEO resigned abruptly (AP).
Grocery Dive, which received the memo, reports that decisions on affected roles will be communicated starting in the coming months, and that no timeline or departments were given.
The memo passages quoted by AP and Grocery Dive speak of 'technology' and efficiency, not of AI by name.
Kroger shares fell 1.6% in morning trading on Tuesday to $61.66 (AP).
Kroger is also in a fight with Albertsons over their failed merger; a trial is slated to start 19 Oct in Delaware (Grocery Dive).
quote_evidence: Grocery store chain Kroger said it will lay off 3,000 corporate employees over the next three years as it ramps up its use of artificial intelligence to streamline operations.
We need to adopt capabilities, reduce duplicative work and look closely at where work is best fit to be done.
Kroger plans to cut its corporate workforce by approximately 3,000 jobs over the next three years, according to a memo from CEO Greg Foran that the grocer shared with Grocery Dive.
why_it_matters_hint: About 3,000 corporate jobs at the largest US standalone supermarket chain are to go over three years, with new technology cited as a reason.
event_date: Memo dated Monday 12 Oct 2026; first reported 13 Oct 2026
notes: The AP page was blocked (HTTP 403); the AP text was read on its wire copy at Bozeman Daily Chronicle and cross-checked with Grocery Dive's own reporting. Memo is dated 12 Oct but the plan was first reported on 13 Oct, so scored as new.
